cards.name: Knight
cards.best_placement: Place defensively in the middle/back of your own side to intercept and tank an incoming ground push, then let it walk into the enemy side as a counter-push tank. On offense, deploy in front of a higher-cost win condition (e.g., a Giant or Hog) to soak tower and troop damage. Avoid placing it deep in a lane where it gets surrounded with no support.
usage_rules: Use it to body-block and kill single-target glass cannons: drop it directly on or in front of an enemy Musketeer or Archers to absorb hits while it kills them.
Do NOT use the Knight alone against swarms (Skeleton Army, Goblin Gang, Minion Horde): it has single-target melee damage and gets overwhelmed. Pair it with a splash unit or a small spell.
Knight cannot hit air. Never rely on it to deal with Minions, Minion Horde, Baby Dragon, or any air troop. Defend air separately.
Deploy reactively, not preemptively: wait until the opponent commits a ground attacker, then place the Knight to intercept so its high HP is not wasted.
As a cheap tank, place it in front of a slower win condition before crossing the bridge so it eats tower shots and defensive single-target troops.
After it survives a defense, push with it: its leftover HP makes it a free tank for a counter-attack. Add support behind it.
If the opponent has a Skeleton Army, Valkyrie, or P.E.K.K.A in cycle, do not send the Knight in unsupported, as those hard-counter it.
Good elixir-positive defensive trade: a 3-elixir Knight can shut down and kill a 4-elixir Musketeer if placed to tank and out-trade it.

cards.name: Archers
cards.best_placement: Behind your tank or building, or at the back of your side of the arena, so they survive to shoot from range. Defensively, place them a few tiles away from the threat (not on top of it) so their two-unit ranged DPS lands before melee or splash reaches them. Keep them split apart against spells when possible since they deploy as two separate units.
usage_rules: Two separate units sharing 3 elixir: never clump them tight next to an opponent who has Arrows, Fireball, or Log ready, because both can die to one spell.
Use as primary air defense vs Minions, Minion Horde, Bats, and Lava Hound balloon-support: they target air and out-range Minions.
Deploy at the back to build a push behind a tank (Giant, Golem) so they pick off air and ranged support from safety.
On defense, place 4-5 tiles back from incoming ground troops (Hog, mini-tank) so they get extra shots before contact and avoid melee retaliation.
Do NOT use them to tank: their HP is low and they die fast to any direct hit or splash.
Do NOT rely on them to counter ground surround-swarms (Skeleton Army, Goblin Gang, Goblins) without splash support; the swarm surrounds and shreds the two low-HP Archers.
Split them across both lanes at the start of a match or in double-elixir to defend two threats or apply chip pressure.
If the opponent has a tank approaching, place Archers slightly behind/beside your own defensive building so the building soaks aggro while Archers free-fire.
Value play: cycle them to defend a cheap air threat and leave survivors to counter-push toward the tower.

cards.name: Goblins
cards.best_placement: Drop them directly on top of, or immediately beside, an incoming ground troop so all three blades reach it at once for maximum melee DPS. Place them surrounding a single-target tank (Giant, Hog, P.E.K.K.A) on the side it is not facing, or on the bridge/your side as a cheap defensive swarm, never out in the open where a splash unit or spell can hit all three. Keep them slightly behind your tower line so you can react to where the threat lands.
usage_rules: Play only when the opponent has NO splash damage or small spell ready (no Arrows, Fireball, Log, or splash troop like Valkyrie/Bomber/Wizard on the field or affordable), since one of those wipes all three for value.

Use defensively against single-target tanks and beefy ground units (Giant, Hog Rider, Prince, Mini P.E.K.K.A, P.E.K.K.A, Goblin Giant): swarm them to shred HP fast; they are a positive elixir trade vs anything 4+ elixir.
Surround the target rather than blocking its path, so the enemy's single hit kills only one Goblin and the other two keep dealing damage.
Do NOT use against air units; Goblins cannot target air, so they are useless versus Minions, Baby Dragon, balloon, or any flyer.
As a chip/offense tool, drop them at the bridge only when the lane is clear and the opponent cannot cheaply answer; three fast melee hitters do high tower damage if ignored.
Do not deploy them spread out or far from the threat; their low individual HP means they must engage immediately and together.
Pair them behind or beside a tank on offense to clear out enemy ground defenders while the tank absorbs hits.
Note: Zap does NOT kill equal-level Goblins (it only stuns/resets them), so Goblins are usable against Zap-reliant decks. Hold them only if the opponent baits with Arrows/Fireball/Log.

cards.name: Giant
cards.best_placement: At the very back behind the King Tower (back corner of your side) when you have an elixir lead, so the Giant reaches the bridge with full elixir regenerated to build a push behind it. Never place it at the bridge raw on defense or with low elixir. Defensively, it can be dropped to body-block, but its real job is offense as the tank that soaks tower damage while support troops behind it deal the actual damage.
usage_rules: Only play Giant when you can afford to support it: never send it alone. It targets buildings/towers only and does not defend itself against troops, so it needs ranged or splash support placed behind it (Musketeer, Witch, Wizard, Archers, Mini P.E.K.K.A).
Play it at the back when your elixir is at or near 10 (full) and you are not under immediate attack, giving you time to add support as it walks up.
Do NOT cycle Giant on defense as a primary blocker against a swarm: it ignores troops and they will surround and kill it while it walks to a building.
Place it on the side opposite the enemy's strongest defensive building or the side with the weaker/already-damaged tower.
If the opponent has an Inferno Tower or Inferno Dragon active, do not commit the Giant until you can zap/snowball/lightning the inferno or pull/distract it, or it melts within seconds.
Use it to soak tower fire while a glass cannon (e.g., Musketeer) sits behind: the tower shoots the Giant, the support troop survives and clears the tower.
Bridge-block on defense only as an emergency: dropping Giant in front of an incoming win condition (e.g., enemy Hog or Royal Giant) buys time, but expect to lose the trade in value.
In a double-elixir or overtime push, lead with Giant and stack two or more support troops behind for a heavy committed push.
Against ground swarms attacking the Giant (Skeleton Army, Goblins, Barbarians), have a splash answer (Arrows, Zap, Valkyrie, Wizard) ready or the Giant push stalls.

cards.name: Mini P.E.K.K.A
cards.best_placement: Defend by dropping it directly onto the incoming ground tank or win-condition (e.g. Giant or Hog Rider) just behind your King Tower / in the center so it locks on and deletes the target fast. After it survives a defense, let it walk to a lane as a counterpush mini-tank, ideally paired with a ranged support (Musketeer/Archers) placed behind it. Do not place it in front at the bridge on offense alone; it has no anti-air and dies to swarms.
usage_rules: Single-target only: never expect it to handle swarms or air. If the enemy push is Skeleton Army, Goblin Gang, Minion Horde, or Minions, do NOT defend with Mini P.E.K.K.A alone; it gets swarmed and killed.
Use as a hard defense vs single big ground units: when enemy plays Giant, Hog Rider, Prince, or Knight, drop it adjacent so it locks on; its high single-target DPS shreds tanks.
It cannot target air. Against Balloon, Minions, Minion Horde, Baby Dragon, etc., it is useless on defense. Keep a separate air answer.

On counterpush, only commit it across the river when you have elixir for support and the enemy has just spent their swarm/spell. A lone Mini P.E.K.K.A at the tower is easily countered by 1-3 elixir of skeletons/goblins.
Pre-place it to intercept fast ground win-conditions (Hog Rider, Battle Ram) before they reach the tower; its fast move speed lets it catch up and one-rotation a Hog.
Keep it out of obvious Tornado/spell value: a spread or pull spell wastes its lockon. Bait the spell first if possible.
Watch elixir: at 4 elixir it is a positive trade against most 5-elixir tanks (Giant) but a negative trade if killed by a 3-elixir swarm. Only deploy when the matchup is a single ground target.
On a bot's checklist: deploy IF (incoming unit is single AND ground AND not a swarm) THEN place on top/just behind it; ELSE hold.

cards.name: Musketeer
cards.best_placement: Deploy at the back of your side (behind the King tower or just in front of it) so she can build up support behind a tank as the push moves up the lane. On defense, place her in the center far enough from the bridge that she is out of enemy spell range while still inside her own attack range of the incoming threat. Against air, place her so the target enters her range before reaching the tower. Keep her well behind the front line and never within a single-spell radius of any other unit.
usage_rules: Single-target high-DPS ranged unit (range ~6 tiles): use her as primary anti-air and anti-tank support, not as a frontline unit.
Play her when the opponent commits an air win-condition (Balloon, Lava Hound, Baby Dragon) or an air swarm she can pick off; she hits both ground and air.

NEVER deploy her within Fireball/Lightning/Rocket radius of another troop or the tower edge; she has only ~340 HP. She survives Fireball at higher levels but is left near death; Lightning and Rocket one-shot her outright.
On defense vs Hog Rider, place her on the opposite side of the Hog's path so she gets extra hits while the tower also fires; she shreds the Hog before it does heavy damage.
Behind-a-tank rule: deploy her behind a Giant/Golem/tank only after the tank has crossed the river or is at your bridge, so she stays protected and out-ranges defenders.
Do not lead a push with her or send her alone across the bridge; she has no splash and folds to any swarm (Skeletons, Goblins, Minion Horde) or melee charge (Mini P.E.K.K.A, Prince, Valkyrie).
If the opponent holds a small spell (Arrows) and your Musketeer is already chipped below ~half HP, pull her back into your zone rather than pushing.
Use her to snipe across lanes only when the target is within her range and no enemy spell is up; otherwise keep her defending.
Value trade: at 4 elixir she defends a 5-6 elixir push and survives to counter-attack, so prioritize keeping her alive over greedy chip.

cards.name: Arrows
cards.best_placement: Cast directly on top of the centroid of a clustered swarm or squishy support troop (Minion Horde, Goblin Gang, Princess). The area-of-effect radius is large, so center the reticle on the densest cluster of low-HP units. When countering a swarm escorting a push, place over the swarm not the tank. Can also be cast on the enemy tower for a few points of chip damage when a kill is otherwise imminent, but this is rarely efficient.
usage_rules: Play Arrows when 3 or more low-HP swarm units (each under ~150 HP) are clustered within the Arrows AoE radius, so the 3 elixir trades up or evenly.
Use to one-shot Minion Horde, Goblins, Spear Goblins, Skeleton Army, Bats, and Fire Spirits; it fully wipes all of these in a single cast.
Use to kill a Princess in one cast (Arrows out-ranges and out-damages her fragile HP), making it the standard hard-counter.
Cast on Minions/Minion Horde once they cross the river and commit to a target, since Arrows hits both air and ground.
Do NOT use Arrows on a single high-HP target (Knight, Valkyrie, Mini P.E.K.K.A, Musketeer) — its damage is too low to kill them and the trade is negative.
Do NOT rely on Arrows to clear Guards: their shields absorb the hit and the skeletons survive a single cast.
Reduce the value loss by waiting until swarm units have grouped tightly; do not fire on a single straggler.
Hold Arrows in cycle if the opponent runs swarm-based win conditions or chip decks (Goblin Barrel splash value, Minion-based air decks).
When defending a Balloon or Lava Hound supported by Minions, use Arrows to clear the air support, not the win condition itself.
Can finish a tower already below the Arrows damage threshold for the kill, but otherwise prefer saving it for swarm defense.

cards.name: Fireball
countered_by: single high-HP tanks (spell does not kill them)
cards.best_placement: Targeted directly on the center of a clumped group of enemy support troops (e.g. behind a tank), or on the tower-side edge of a group to also chip the Crown Tower. Aim where the troops will be when the projectile lands, accounting for its travel time, not where they currently are.
usage_rules: Cast on 2 or more clustered medium-HP support troops (Musketeer, Wizard, Witch, Flying Machine) to one-shot or near-kill them and gain a positive elixir trade.
Use to wipe Minion Horde or Goblin Gang only when they are tightly clumped; Fireball's radius covers most of a clump but spread troops may survive.
Fireball does NOT one-shot Barbarians at equal level; they survive a single cast. Pair Fireball with Zap/Log or use a bigger spell to clear them.
Three Musketeers are only Fireballed cleanly when clumped; the standard split-lane play deliberately spreads them so one Fireball cannot hit all three.
Do NOT waste on a single low-cost troop (e.g. one Archer, one Goblin) since the spell costs 4 and gives a negative trade.
Use as a finisher on an enemy Crown Tower when the tower is below roughly Fireball's damage in remaining HP, especially in double/triple elixir or overtime.
Lead the target: release the cast slightly ahead of moving troops so the projectile lands on them after its ~1 second travel time.
Do NOT use Fireball as a primary answer to single tanks (Giant, Golem, P.E.K.K.A); it only chips them and is a poor trade.
Hold Fireball defensively against a known glass-cannon push rather than spending it on chip if the opponent relies on squishy support behind a tank.

cards.name: Spear Goblins
counters: lone low-HP air troops without splash
countered_by: any splash unit (Valkyrie, Wizard, Baby Dragon, Bomber)
cards.best_placement: Drop them in the back behind your tank or a few tiles behind the King Tower so they survive the first enemy contact and chip from range as the push advances. To defend, place them spread out behind your tower (not in a tight clump) so a single splash spell or splash troop cannot wipe all three, and so they can shoot air attackers crossing the bridge. Never place them in front as a damage soak; they have almost no HP.
usage_rules: Three units, ground troops, ranged attack that hits both ground and air. Each goblin has very low HP (dies to almost any damage) and low per-hit damage, but they fire from range.

Play them defensively against a single low-HP air troop with no splash, where they can chip it from range. They do NOT counter high-HP air (Lava Hound) or building-targeting air (Balloon), which ignore them and out-last their low DPS.
Use them as a cheap (2 elixir) ranged support behind a tank to add chip DPS to a push without committing much elixir.

Do NOT play them into the open against an opponent who is holding Arrows, Zap, The Log, or any splash unit (Valkyrie, Bomber, Wizard, Baby Dragon). All three die to one Arrows/Fireball, and Zap/Log kills or heavily damages them.
Spread the three units apart on defense so one splash hit cannot kill all three at once.
Good positive-elixir trade when they chip down or finish a higher-cost unit before dying.
Use them to finish off a weakened tower or to pick off a low-HP unit from range while staying behind your own troops.
Avoid sending them alone across the bridge as a lone offense; they have too little HP to threaten a tower before being cleared, but they are fine as ride-along chip behind a tank.
Treat them as expendable: their value is cheap ranged chip and air harassment, not survivability.

cards.name: Bomber
cards.best_placement: Place behind a tank (Giant, Knight, or Valkyrie) so the tank absorbs damage while Bomber lobs area splash over the tank onto swarms and the tower. As a defensive card, drop it a few tiles behind your own tower or in the center so it has time to acquire incoming ground swarms before they reach it, keeping its fragile body out of direct enemy fire.
usage_rules: Deploy Bomber against any ground swarm (Skeleton Army, Goblin Gang, Skeletons, Goblins, Spear Goblins) — its area splash one-shots or two-shots most low-hp ground units and gives heavy positive elixir trades.
NEVER use Bomber against air: it cannot target flying units (Minions, Minion Horde, Bats, Baby Dragon) — if the enemy push contains air, pair Bomber with an air-targeting troop or do not rely on it.
Bomber's splash does NOT cleanly clear Barbarians; they out-HP and out-damage it. Use a bigger splash answer for Barbarians.
Always keep Bomber behind a tank or your tower; with low hp it dies to a single Fireball or one melee swing from Knight/Valkyrie/Mini P.E.K.K.A — never let it tank.
Use Bomber as the splash support behind a win condition (Giant + Bomber, Hog + Bomber) so it clears the defending swarm while the tank pushes the tower.
Do not commit Bomber when the opponent holds a small spell (Arrows, Fireball, Zap-into-followup): grouping it with other troops makes it spell-bait value for them.
On defense, place Bomber centrally so it can fire on either lane and so its slow-traveling lob connects before swarms overrun it.

Trigger condition a bot can check: if incoming threat == ground swarm (>=3 cheap units) AND no enemy air unit present AND Bomber is in hand AND elixir >= 3, deploy Bomber 3-4 tiles in front of the targeted tower.
Trigger condition: if a friendly tank is on the field pushing AND Bomber is in hand, place Bomber 1 tile behind the tank to convert it into a splash push.

cards.name: Skeletons
counters: Lone melee tanks (e.g. P.E.K.K.A, Giant when no support)
countered_by: any splash damage troop or spell
cards.best_placement: Drop directly on top of, or just in front of, a single-target ground attacker (Mini P.E.K.K.A, Prince, Hog Rider) to surround it and trade 1 elixir for a multi-elixir threat. For pure cycle, place at the back near the King Tower / bridge-side lane to cheaply rotate to your win condition. Never place spread out in the open where one splash card kills all three.
usage_rules: Play only against SINGLE-TARGET GROUND units; never use as the primary answer to anything that does splash damage or hits air.
Use to distract and reset a charging Prince or Mini P.E.K.K.A: surround it so its single-target hits kill one skeleton at a time while the tower or another unit finishes it.
Use as a cheap cycle card (1 elixir) to get back to your win condition faster when ahead on elixir or rotating.
Pair with a building or tank-killer to chunk a lone tank (e.g. surround a P.E.K.K.A or Hog Rider so it kills one skeleton per swing).
Do NOT deploy if the opponent has a cheap splash answer ready in cycle (Zap, Log, Arrows) and you would gain nothing; three skeletons die to all of those.
Hold this card if the only incoming threat is air or a splash unit; it provides zero value there.
Skeletons cannot hit air, so they cannot deal with Mega Minion or any flyer.
Kite ground tanks toward your King Tower by placing on the opposite side to pull and stall.
Deploy at the bridge to chip an undefended tower only when the opponent has no troops and no cheap splash to respond; value is marginal so prefer cycle/defense use.

cards.name: Minions
counters: Lone ground troops that cannot hit air
cards.best_placement: Deploy directly on top of the enemy ground unit you want to swarm (e.g. on a Giant, Hog, or Mini P.E.K.K.A pushing your tower) so all 3 attack immediately; or behind your own tank as cheap chip air support. As an air defender, place ahead of incoming air troops like Balloon so they lock on before it reaches the tower. Never deploy clustered in the open against a player holding Arrows/Zap.
usage_rules: Three flying units that attack both ground and air; total HP is low so any AoE spell threatens all three at once.
Play defensively on ground tanks/win-conditions with no air-targeting support (Giant, Hog Rider, Royal Giant, Mini P.E.K.K.A): drop on top of the unit to maximize DPS and stack damage.

Do NOT deploy if the opponent likely holds Arrows or Zap (both one-shot or near-kill all three for 3 or 2 elixir, a positive trade for them). Hold Minions until their spell is spent or commit only when the value (e.g. killing a Balloon) outweighs the spell loss.

To counter air win-conditions like Balloon, place Minions ahead of its path with lead time so all three lock on before it reaches the tower; dropped on top after it is already over the tower they often fail.
On offense, pair behind a tank as cheap chip damage, but expect them to die to Arrows/Fireball; only send when the spell cycle is unfavorable for the opponent.
Avoid sending Minions alone across the river against towers/Princess Towers; the tower out-damages them and they die before getting value.
Do not use Minions against splash-air units (Baby Dragon, Wizard, Witch, Executioner) without support, as splash erases all three quickly.
Do not expect Minions to win the air 1v1 against Mega Minion; it out-trades a fresh set.

cards.name: Valkyrie
cards.best_placement: Defensively, place her directly on top of or right next to a swarm/support troop so her 360-degree spin attack hits the whole group at once; deploy in the center or just behind the bridge-side of your King Tower to intercept ground pushes. Offensively, drop her behind a tank (Giant, Golem) at the back as a secondary damage dealer and ground-swarm clearer, or use her to soak tower hits while support troops do damage.
usage_rules: Only deploy against GROUND targets. Never play her to defend air units (Minions, Minion Horde, Baby Dragon, Balloon, Lava Hound) because she cannot attack air.
When the enemy commits a ground swarm (Skeleton Army, Goblins, Goblin Gang, Barbarians), place her in the MIDDLE of the swarm so her area-of-effect spin hits all units in one rotation.

If the opponent has a glass-cannon ground support unit (Musketeer, Wizard, Witch, Princess, Dart Goblin) walking with a tank, send Valkyrie to body-block; she kills the squishy support only if she reaches it (ranged units can kite and chip her), so back her with a tank.
Do NOT play her in the open when the opponent likely holds Fireball, Poison, or Lightning if other troops are clustered near her; her medium damage push is easy spell value.
Use her as a mini-tank in front of ranged support (Musketeer, Archers) on offense: she absorbs tower and troop damage while the ranged units deal DPS from behind.
After she survives a defense with significant HP remaining, support her with a ranged troop and push the opposite lane for a counter-attack.
Against a lone Goblin Barrel or Skeleton Army on your tower, she clears it cleanly and cheaply if pre-placed or reacted to in time.
Do not use her alone as a primary win condition; her damage to towers is too low. Pair her with a real win-condition or use her purely for defense plus counter-push value.

cards.name: Baby Dragon
cards.best_placement: Place it behind your King Tower or Arena Tower at the back so it builds up elixir advantage and arrives at the bridge with full HP, letting it tank for and support a push. Defensively, drop it near the center of your side to splash down incoming swarms and air units, then it counterpushes. As a flying unit it ignores ground obstacles and pathing, so it can be placed to lock onto the nearest threat from any lane.
usage_rules: Play it when the opponent commits a swarm of low-HP units (Skeleton Army, Goblin Gang, Minion Horde, Bats); its area splash damage wipes most of them in 1-2 hits.
Deploy it against air units (Minions, Minion Horde, balloon support) since it targets both ground and air; most lower-arena air defense is limited, making this its key value.
Start it at the back of your side (behind King Tower) when you have a full or near-full elixir bar and no immediate threat, to begin a slow building push.
Pair it in front of or behind a tank (Giant) once it reaches the bridge so it splashes the defending swarm while the tank absorbs tower fire.
Do NOT send it alone at a tower expecting big damage; its single-target DPS is medium and it will be out-damaged by a Musketeer, Mega Minion, or Inferno Tower.
Do NOT rely on its splash to clear Barbarians or Guards: Barbarians out-HP and out-DPS a lone Baby Dragon, and Guards' shields absorb the splash.
Against a Princess, note she massively out-ranges the Baby Dragon (~9 vs ~3.5 tiles) and can kite it, so it is only a situational answer.
Avoid playing it when the opponent holds a Fireball or has a Musketeer/Inferno ready, as those trade up or hard-counter it.

cards.name: Hog Rider
counters: slow ground pushes (Giant, Golem) by punishing the opposite lane
cards.best_placement: Deploy at the bridge in whichever lane the opponent has the fewest defensive troops, ideally on the side away from a defensive building. A common technique is placing it one tile back from the bridge so it crosses and locks onto the tower before slower defenders can line up, or in the opposite lane to a defensive building so it does not get pulled. Apply it when the opponent is low on elixir or has just committed a big push in the other lane.
usage_rules: Only targets buildings: it ignores all troops and walks straight to the nearest building or tower, so play it when the opponent has no active defensive building down (no Cannon/Tombstone/Tesla/Bomb Tower on the field).
Play it at the bridge when the opponent is at or below ~4 elixir and cannot afford a swarm response.
Punish in the opposite lane: if the opponent commits a slow tank push (Giant/Golem/P.E.K.K.A) on one side, send Hog Rider on the other lane immediately for a counterattack.
Do NOT send it naked into a known defensive building in that lane; a Cannon or Tombstone pulls it to center and kills it for a positive trade. Bait or destroy the building first.

Watch for swarm counters: if the opponent holds Skeleton Army, Goblin Gang, Barbarians, or Minion Horde, pair the Hog with a small splash unit (Zap, Arrows, Fireball, Valkyrie) ready to clear the swarm.
Use as a fast cycle/chip card: at very-fast speed it reaches the tower quickly, so chip damage accumulates even when defended for one or two hits.
If the opponent has a building placed in the center (anti-Hog placement), redirect by deploying Hog so its pathing still reaches a tower, or switch to the lane the building cannot cover.
Best when supported: a Hog behind nothing is fine for chip, but combine with Ice Spirit, Skeletons, or a Zap to disable/reset the defending troop and let the Hog connect for extra hits.

cards.name: Wizard
cards.best_placement: Behind the tank or behind the King Tower as a defensive anchor, so he survives to throw splash fireballs at incoming swarms; on offense, place him a few tiles behind your win condition (e.g. behind a Giant) so the tank absorbs damage while the Wizard clears the swarms and air defenders meant to stop the tank. Never place him in front where he eats direct hits.
usage_rules: Play him when the opponent commits a swarm of 3 or more low-HP units (Skeleton Army, Goblin Gang, Minion Horde): his area splash one-shots most of them.
Play him to defend against air: he targets both ground and air, so deploy him against Minions, Minion Horde, Bats, or Baby Dragon.

Do NOT play him in the open against a known Fireball/Lightning/Poison cycle when grouped with other troops; though a single Fireball does NOT kill a full-HP Wizard (he has Musketeer-tier HP), the value trade still favors the opponent. Wait for them to spend their splash spell first.
Place him at least 4 tiles back from the front line so he isn't reached by Mini P.E.K.K.A, Knight, Valkyrie, or Prince, which one-shot or quickly melt him in melee.
Use him as a defensive support behind a tank troop on a push rather than as a standalone offensive unit; alone he is slow.
He counters the Hog Rider: the Hog only targets buildings and ignores him while his splash shreds it.
Pair him with a tank: let the tank soak tower/troop damage while the Wizard provides splash DPS from behind.
Against a lone medium-HP attacker (Mini P.E.K.K.A, Musketeer) do not rely on Wizard alone: he loses the 1v1, so add a distraction or chip building.

cards.name: Barbarians
cards.best_placement: Defensively, in the center of your side just behind the bridge/king tower line so all four spawn and surround an incoming ground attacker (split-pincer the tank). For pushes, place at the back behind the king tower to build a slow, high-DPS swarm push, ideally paired with a tank in front to absorb splash. Never drop them clumped at the bridge into an enemy that has a splash card or Fireball ready.
usage_rules: Deploy defensively when the enemy commits a single high-HP ground unit with no splash support (Giant, Royal Giant, Hog Rider, Prince, Mini P.E.K.K.A, Battle Ram): surround it for a fast, near-free kill.
Only play if you have 5+ elixir AND will not be left below ~3 elixir against a known splash/Fireball follow-up, since all 4 Barbarians die to Fireball+small-spell or to splash.
Do NOT deploy against air units. Barbarians are ground-only and target ground; air troops (Minions, Mega Minion, Baby Dragon, Balloon, Minion Horde) are immune to them.

Do NOT clump them where a single Fireball, Arrows-finish, Valkyrie, Bomber, or Wizard can hit multiple at once. If the enemy holds an unused splash spell, split deployment or use a different defender.
Use as a counter-push: after they survive defending a tank, push them with a fresh tank in front so the tank eats splash and Barbarians deal DPS to the tower.
Place to intercept and body-block win conditions before they reach the tower; their high combined DPS deletes lone tanks quickly when all four connect.
Avoid offense into a full enemy hand with no chip lead; the 5-elixir cost makes a Fireball/Poison value trade punishing.
Against Skeleton Army or other swarm, prefer a splash card instead. Barbarians trade poorly clump-vs-clump.
If the enemy uses a Tornado or pull spell, expect Barbarians to be grouped and Fireballed. Hold them until the spell is spent.

cards.name: Goblin Hut
counters: lone glass-cannon support (Musketeer, Wizard) over time
cards.best_placement: Center of your side, roughly on or just behind the river-to-tower midline (around 3-4 tiles in front of and between your two towers), so the spawned Spear Goblins reach the most ground while the hut itself pulls and distracts pushes coming down either lane. Pull it slightly toward the side under attack to defend a specific lane, but keep it centered for steady chip pressure. Never place it at the bridge or on the enemy side.
usage_rules: The Goblin Hut is a spawner that does NOT attack; post-rework (May 2025) it costs 4 elixir, has a 30s lifetime, and is REACTIVE: it only spawns when an enemy enters its ~6-tile sight range, deploying ONE Spear Goblin per wave (not a pair, and not the old three).
Because it is reactive, a back placement with no enemy nearby spawns nothing while its lifetime ticks down; place it where enemy pushes will come so it actually spawns.
The Spear Goblins it spawns target air and ground, so it provides slow chip pressure and helps against air; do not rely on it to block or tank a push by itself.
Do not deploy it when the opponent holds Fireball or Poison ready and your other troops are clustered near it, since one spell can value-trade the hut plus spawns.
Do not place it directly in a push's path expecting it to body-block; for a pure distraction/defensive building Cannon or Tesla is better.
Use the Spear Goblins it spawns as a support stream behind your own win condition once it has fired a few waves on defense.
Do not answer the hut with Lightning or Rocket: at 6 elixir against a 4-elixir building these are heavy negative trades. Use a small splash spell or splash troop instead.
If the opponent commits a glass-cannon (Musketeer/Wizard) alone near your tower, the spawned Spear Goblins plus tower fire can overwhelm it; bait the spell first if possible.
